SugarCraft\Minesweeper

Board final class

The minesweeper board — pure value object. Immutable; every reveal or flag returns a fresh Board with the changed cells swapped in.

MethodSummary
static fromRows(int $width, int $height, int $mineCount, array $rows, bool $minesPlaced = false, bool $exploded = false, int $revealedCount = 0, int $flaggedCount = 0): selfPublic direct-construction boundary: the grid census for callers that hand us a full $rows map. Fail fast on a misshapen grid: a 5×5-claim over 2×2 data would silently produce an un-winnable board (win threshold unreachable, reveals outside the real data no-op). unserialize() runs its own stricter wire pass and constructs directly; both honour the same promise.
static blank(int $width, int $height, int $mineCount): selfEmpty board — all cells unrevealed, no mines. The first reveal triggers mine placement, avoiding the clicked cell + its eight neighbours whenever the mine count leaves room (so the player gets a non-trivial flood-fill on click 1). A board dense enough that the exclusion would starve the placement falls back to keeping only the clicked cell mine-free — see placeMines(). That regime is unreachable through the CLI: the launcher caps mines at cells − 9.
cell(int $x, int $y): ?Cell
rows(): array
reveal(int $x, int $y, \Closure $rand): selfReveal the cell at (x, y). If it has no adjacent mines, also reveal every neighbour transitively (classic flood fill). If mines aren't yet placed, place them first, excluding the clicked cell's 3×3 neighbourhood — or, on a board too dense for that exclusion to leave enough candidates, the clicked cell alone (placeMines()).
cycleMarker(int $x, int $y): self
isWon(): boolTrue exactly when every non-mine cell has been revealed. O(1) via revealedCount.
flagCount(): intNumber of flagged cells. O(1) via the incrementally-tracked counter.
serialize(): stringSerialize the board to a string for save/load mid-game.
static unserialize(string $data): selfReconstruct a Board from a string produced by serialize().
chord(int $x, int $y): selfChord click — reveal all unflagged neighbours of a "satisfied" number.

Game final class

Minesweeper as a SugarCraft Model. Keys: - arrows / hjkl → move cursor - space / enter → reveal - f → toggle flag - c → chord - S → save the live game (single slot, 0600, under $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/candy-minesweeper/ when that env is set, else $HOME/.config/candy-minesweeper/) - L → load that save — works even after game over, so the player can step a lost board back to the saved one - r → restart - n → new-game picker: 1-4 start a preset, c opens the custom-board digit form, q/Esc walk back - q / esc / Ctrl+C → quit (q/Esc ask twice on a live unsaved board) Mouse: left-click reveals, right-click flags, middle-click chords.

Not listed: the methods of SugarCraft\Core\Concerns\Mutable, a trait declared outside src/.

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly Board $board, public readonly int $cursorX = 0, public readonly int $cursorY = 0, ?\Closure $rand = null, public readonly ?float $startedAt = null, public readonly ?int $elapsedSeconds = null, public readonly ?Stats $stats = null, public readonly ?string $statsPath = null, public readonly ?string $notice = null, public readonly bool $newBest = false, public readonly ?int $beatenRecord = null, public readonly int $frameCols = 80, public readonly int $frameRows = 24, public readonly bool $restoredGame = false, public readonly bool $dirty = false, public readonly bool $confirmQuit = false, public readonly bool $picking = false, public readonly ?CustomForm $form = null, public readonly ?float $lastClickAt = null, public readonly int $lastClickX = -1, public readonly int $lastClickY = -1)
requiredRows(): intTerminal rows the current frame consumes: board height, the rounded border (2), the status line (1), the four-line help footer, and a spare line — plus one more while a toast rides above the status. Below this the board cannot be shown whole, and the game refuses rather than painting a clipped minefield.
tooSmall(): boolTrue when the live terminal cannot host the full frame.
withFrame(int $cols, int $rows): selfSeed the live viewport at boot (the runtime then owns updates).
withPicker(): selfOpen the new-game picker overlay on this game's board: the opt-in --pick launch lands here, so the first frame is the same overlay n opens mid-game. The board underneath is the plain 10x10 default, which is also where q/Esc walk back to, so the picker is a door in front of the unchanged launch contract rather than a different one.
static start(int $width = 10, int $height = 10, int $mines = 12, ?\Closure $rand = null, ?Stats $stats = null, ?string $statsPath = null, ?string $notice = null): self
static withDifficulty(Difficulty $d, ?\Closure $rand = null, ?Stats $stats = null, ?string $statsPath = null, ?string $notice = null): self
static withCustom(int $width, int $height, int $mines, ?\Closure $rand = null, ?Stats $stats = null, ?string $statsPath = null, ?string $notice = null): selfConvenience alias of start() for named-argument call sites ("custom" dimensions vs the preset ladder). Deliberately carries no validation of its own — callers coming from user input route through \SugarCraft\Minesweeper\Ui\CustomDifficulty::fromInput() first (the CLI does), which is what makes the alias safe to keep.
difficulty(): ?Difficulty
rand(): \ClosureThe injected PRNG. Exposed because Board::reveal() takes the closure per call — a caller cloning a Game (or driving the Board directly, as the save round-trip pins do) must reuse this game's sequence rather than silently switching to random_int.
stats(): Stats
init(): ?\Closure
update(Msg $msg): array
static presetKeys(): arrayThe picker's digit → preset table in display order (msw-09). One source for both the renderer's rows and the model's key handling: a re-ordered enum can never make key 2 start what the screen labelled 3 (finding 058's same-table-different-meaning class).
static savePath(): ?stringAbsolute path of the single-slot savegame, resolved from the environment at call time (never cached — tests sandbox HOME per test, and a process that learned its HOME after boot should still find the file). XDG_CONFIG_HOME wins when set AND absolute; a relative value is ignored and the slot falls to $HOME/.config (finding -064: the docblock promises an absolute path, and a relative XDG leg would make the slot CWD-dependent — the XDG spec bars relative values too). Null when neither carries a usable value: save then degrades to a no-op and load keeps the current game, mirroring the best-effort stats writes.
view(): string
elapsed(): ?floatElapsed seconds: the live wall clock while the game runs, the frozen $elapsedSeconds stamp once it is over (set at the transition or restored from a finished save), null before the first reveal.
recordResult(?float $elapsed): selfRecord the result of this game and return a new Game with updated stats. The returned Game has the same board state but updated stats.
subscriptions(): ?\SugarCraft\Core\SubscriptionsArm the 1 Hz 'clock' tick while — and only while — the timer is live: from the first actual reveal (startedAt set; dud keypresses and refused clicks never arm it) to the win/lose transition (board over, elapsed frozen into elapsedSeconds). The runtime reconciles subscriptions after every update cycle, so the tick starts on the first reveal and is cancelled when this method stops listing the id.

SugarCraft\Minesweeper\Support

Requirements final class

Boot requirements as data (msw-23, finding candy-minesweeper-018). The app rides sugar-core's cell-width and i18n math, whose own manifest declares ext-intl + ext-mbstring (sugar-core/composer.json:34-35). The composer path enforces them transitively, but the advertised phar channel installs nothing through composer — without a preflight the first frame that measures a glyph would semi-die on an undefined-function Error laundered out of frozen vendor code.

Version final class

The version string this tool reports on --version.

MethodSummary
static line(): stringThe --version line: plain text, newline-terminated, produced by no state and no host probe — the flag must answer anywhere.
static current(): stringThe version this process reports: the archive stamp when running from a stamped phar, self::CURRENT everywhere else.
static fromPharMetadata(string $path): ?stringThe version a phar archive at $path was built to carry, or null when it names none (unreadable archive, wrong metadata shape, the dev-build sentinel, or an empty stamp). Every refusal is a null, never an exception — --version must answer on a machine whose phar cannot be opened.
static versionFromMetadata(mixed $metadata): ?stringThe judgement on the stamp itself, split out because the archive-open leg is unreachable from a suite that must not build phars: the release namespace strip, the dev-build refusal, and the wrong-type nulls are a pure function over what getMetadata() answers.
static hostArchive(): stringThe filesystem path of the phar this process was launched from, or '' when it was not launched from one — measured on candy-code's real builds and pinned by the bin autoload guard: inside archive-loaded code Phar::running(false) answers the archive path, while the stub context answers '' and there a '.phar'-suffixed __DIR__ is the enclosing archive.

SugarCraft\Minesweeper\Ui

CustomDifficulty final class

Board-shape validator + the backing store of the in-game custom-board form (msw-09/G5-b): the picker's CustomForm collects the digits and submits through fromInput(), so the player-specified rows, columns and mine count of a custom game really are validated here — the CLI positional door and the interactive door share one law.

CustomForm final class

The in-game custom-board form state (msw-09/G5-b): three digit fields — width, height, mines — typed one field at a time, submitted through CustomDifficulty::fromInput() so the interactive door and the CLI positional door share one validation law (msw-18).
